title: Spa bather warnings, health exclusions and supervision
audience: Pool and spa service workers, attendants and operators at public spa pools in SA. Figures and warnings apply under the state standard.
learningOutcomes: Describe the bather warning notice that has to sit right beside a public spa, and why each point is there.
Explain the heat, infection and drowning risks that the warnings control.
Check the notice and the supervision arrangements before a spa is opened.

instruction.heading: Where the warning notice goes
instruction.body: A bather warning notice has to be posted somewhere eye-catching right beside the spa, where anyone about to get in can read it. A notice placed out of sight, behind furniture or away from the entry does not meet that purpose. Check the notice every time you open or inspect the spa, and replace it if it is faded, damaged or missing.

instruction.heading: The points the notice must convey
instruction.body: Bathers should keep their heads out of the water. Anyone affected by drugs or alcohol must stay out, and no single session may run longer than 20 minutes. Children may only use the spa under supervision. Swallowing spa water is not permitted. Anyone with an open wound, anyone feeling unwell, and anyone pregnant should keep out of the spa. Each point controls a specific risk, so the notice is a safety control and must stay legible and complete.

instruction.heading: Why these points matter
instruction.body: Head immersion and swallowing water carry infection risk, because warm aerated water can hold high microbial loads. Heat stress builds with high temperatures and long exposure, especially for people with heart conditions or a predisposition to stress. Children can slip under the surface or get into difficulty unobserved. Open wounds give organisms a route in. The 20-minute limit reduces the cumulative heat and exposure load.

instruction.heading: Supervision and refusing entry
instruction.body: The operator must make sure children are supervised whenever they use a public spa. Attendants have authority to deny entry where a person appears unwell, under the influence, or otherwise likely to be at risk, and the standard supports that approach for waterslides and spas alike. Escalate repeated breaches to the operator, and record the incident.

procedure: Confirm the warning notice is present, legible and immediately beside the spa entry.
Check that the notice lists all the points described in the standard.
Confirm the supervision arrangements, including for children, are recorded in the operator plan.
Check the spa temperature and disinfectant before admitting bathers.
Record the check, and report any missing notice or supervision gap to the operator before the spa opens.

workedExamples.situation: A public spa has a warning notice behind a potted plant, around the corner from the entry. A parent is letting a seven-year-old use the spa alone while they change.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What must be done, and by whom?
workedExamples.reasoning: The notice is not right beside the spa and so does not do its job, and the child is unsupervised, which the notice prohibits. Ask the parent to supervise or leave the spa, move the notice to the entry, and escalate to the operator in writing.

equipmentAndPpe: Spare warning notice in good condition
Record sheet for spa checks and incidents
Non-slip footwear around the spa edge

commonErrors.error: Placing the notice out of sight, away from the entry.
commonErrors.prevention: Place it immediately beside the spa, where it is read before entry.

commonErrors.error: Treating the 20-minute limit as a suggestion.
commonErrors.prevention: Enforce the limit as the notice states, and record breaches.

commonErrors.error: Assuming supervision of children is optional at a spa.
commonErrors.prevention: Children must be supervised. Refuse entry where this is not met.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Head immersion, swallowing water and entry with an open wound carry infection risk. Keep the notice in place and enforce it.
Heat stress from high temperature or long exposure is a risk for people with heart conditions. Spa temperature must be controlled.
Figures and notice content are South Australian standard values (revised 2013). Confirm the current regulation text.

qualityStandard: The warning notice is present, legible and right beside the spa entry at each check.
Supervision arrangements for children are recorded and followed.
Refused entries and breaches are recorded with date and action.
documentationEvidence: Spa daily check record including notice status and supervision
Incident or refusal record with time and action
summary: The warning notice is a safety control. Place it immediately beside the spa.
It covers head immersion, alcohol and drugs, the 20-minute limit, child supervision, swallowing water, and health exclusions.
Refuse entry where a bather is unwell, unsupervised as required, or otherwise at risk.

knowledgeChecks.question: Where must the bather warning notice for a public spa be placed?
options: In the office, for staff to read and the staff sign it
Right beside the spa, so it is read before entry
Behind the pool equipment room door and out of sight
On the car park sign only and on the pool gate sign

knowledgeChecks.question: Which of the following is part of the standard's spa bather warning?
options: Bathers may stay in the spa as long as they like
Bathers should keep their heads out of the water
Bathers may swallow spa water in moderation
Children may enter the spa with no adult watching

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the maximum time the standard's warning notice gives for a single spa session?
